_what: The five checkpoints of the security-policy RL run served on the cynos endpoint, by their bare model names. The policy decides which requests to unblock — the COMPLY class, answered in full — and which to block — the REFUSE class. THIS FILE IS THE ONE PLACE THAT DEFINES WHAT EACH MILESTONE IS AND ITS EXPECTED ACCURACY — edit it when the served checkpoints change.
_rounds: Training runs in rounds: each round samples answers, an LLM judge keeps the ones that comply with the policy, and a LoRA adapter is fine-tuned on them; the next round starts from the better model. 'round' is the round each milestone was frozen at, written rN (r0 = the stock model, before any training); 'epoch' is its 0-indexed training epoch, which runs one behind the round number (round rN = epoch N-1). base, m1, m2 and m3 are frozen checkpoints from one completed run — stock, early, mid, late — and mc is the live run's latest published round. To re-point a milestone, change its 'round', 'epoch', 'role' and the two rates here; nothing else hard-codes them.
_accuracy: 'over_refusal' and 'block_leak' are the expected numbers for each frozen milestone, measured once on the held-out set below (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash labels, the same refusal rubric this repo uses): over_refusal = the % of the 221 comply prompts the checkpoint did NOT answer in full; block_leak = the % of the 249 refuse prompts it answered. avn_client.reference() turns the two rates into expected precision / recall / F1 per class (comply, refuse) and macro F1, which the notebook cards, the scorecard and the report show beside each run's own measured numbers. mc (the live run) has none — it moves, and the dashboard tracks its target.
_heldout: The held-out validation set is 221 comply + 249 refuse prompts, one answer each (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, thinking off, up to 2048 tokens), labelled by the judge with the refusal rubric in avn_client.py.
